Order 
This case was heard finally and reserved for orders on 13/12/2024.

This Misc. Appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 12/02/2008 passed in MACC No.01/2007 (Smt. Sumitrabai & others vs. Billu @ Praveen Singh & others) by the Additional Member, MACT Panna (MP) wherein the claim petition filed by the appellants on account of death of Sanjeev S/o Nonelal aged about 11 years has been dismissed 3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The facts of the case in short are that on 17/07/2006 at about 03:00 PM when deceased Sanjeev was returning from the school at that time offending vehicle bearing registration No. MP-16C 0332 being driven by non-applicant No.1 Billu @ Praveen Singh S/o NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:11617 2 MA-2698-2008 Rambabu Singh rashly and negligently and dashed against Sanjeev, wherein he has sustained serious injuries.
Thereafter, deceased was taken to the hospital for treatment but during the course of treatment, he had died.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the vehicle was registered in the name of Abhilash Kumar (non-applicant No.2) and some days prior to the accident allegedly sold to Sanjeev Singh S/o Ram Babu who is the real brother of Billu @ Praveen Singh by the owner of the vehicle i.e.

1 Abhilash Kumar.

sentences.text: The grounds of the appeal are that the evidence and facts have not been properly considered by the Tribunal.
The Police has registered the case, therefore compensation should have been granted.
6. On the other hand, Smt. Amrit Ruprah, learned counsel for respondent No.3 supported the award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

7. In the trial Court, claimants have exhibited First Information Report (Ex.P/1), Spot Map (Ex.P/2),
Post Mortem Report (Ex.P/3) Proof of treatment (Ex.P/4) and Copy of supurdginama (Ex.P/5)
wherein the vehicle has been taken on Supurdginama by Abhilash, Driving License (Ex.P/6) and charge-sheet (Ex.P/7).
8. The applicants have examined the witness Sumitra Bai, mother of the deceased (AW-1), her statement is not doubtful.

A.W.- 
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:11617 3 MA-2698-2008 2
Gopal has supported the case of the claimants. AW-3 Nonelal father of the deceased who has stated in para-8 of his cross- examination that he was not present on the spot at the time of accident.

Gopal S/o Parvat has been mentioned in the charge-sheet as an eye-witness who has deposed in Tribunal as A.W.-2 also,
therefore regarding factum of accident by which Sanjeev died arising out of the motor accident case is not doubtful.
9.

Recently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case Ranjeet & another vs. Abdul Kayam Neb &
another [SLP( C ) No.10351/2019 dated 25/02/2025 has held thus :-
"4.

entities.text:
Ranjeet & another vs. Abdul Kayam Neb &
another [SLP( C ) No.10351/2019
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is settled in law that once a charge-sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.
Even if the eye- witnesses are not examined, that will not be fatal to prove the death of the deceased due to negligence of the bus driver."
(Emphasis supplied)  10. In light of the aforesaid judgment, no further prove in this regard is required regarding factum of accident.

Accordingly, reversing the findings of learned Tribunal regarding accident, it is held that Sanjeev died in a motor accident dated 17/07/2006 when non-applicant No.1 Billu @ Praveen Singh driven the offending vehicle rashly and negligently and hit Sanjeev (deceased)
causing his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:11617 4 MA-2698-2008 death.
11. Regarding that at the time of incident, vehicle was insured with non-applicant No.3 IFFCO TOKIO Insurance Company or not, it is seen that Insurance Policy is not filed.
Date of accident was 17/07/2006.

Before the learned Tribunal, non-applicant No.4- Sanjeev Singh S/o Rambabu Singh has submitted that he has purchased the Smt.Sumitra Bai vs Billu @ Praveen Singh on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150778270/
2 offending vehicle from non-applicant No.2 Abhilash Kumar but he had got the vehicle insured in the name of Abhilash Kumar Tiwari was also deposed the same but on the other side, Tarunesh Kumar Pandey, Development Officer of IFFCO TOKIO Insurance Company and Manoj Kumar Pandey, Agent of IFFCO TOKIO Insurance Company have been examined before the Tribunal and have lead the evidence that on the date of accident vehicle was not insured because on perusal of the statement of these officers, it seems that cover note was cancelled as soon as it had come into the notice of Insurance Company that it has been obtained by fraud making it antedated with the help of one of the staff of Insurance Company i.e. Sunil Kumar, therefore.

entities.text: Smt.Sumitra Bai vs Billu @ Praveen Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, liability cannot be imposed on Insurance Company.
As a consequence, when vehicle was not insured on the date of accident, Insurances Company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, the Insurance Company is exonerated.

12. It is directed that non-applicant No.1 Billu @ Praveen NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:11617 5 MA-2698-2008 Singh, non-applicant No.2 Abhilash Kumar Tiwari and non-applicant No.4 Sanjeev Singh S/o Rambabu Singh are liable to satisfy the award jointly and severally.
13. Now the only question remains is regarding the proper award.

At the time of death, deceased was 11 years, therefore it is directed that non-applicants No. 1, 2 & 4 to pay jointly and separately compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- on lumpsum basis and rate of interest shall be @ 6% from the date of award i.e. 12/02/2008 till payment of compensation.
14.
With the aforesaid observation, the Misc. Appeal stands disposed of (AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE mc Smt.Sumitra Bai vs Billu @ Praveen Singh on 10 March, 2025
